answer: Clone markets mint lookalike agents at near-zero cost. A new key must first cut one marble identity tile, thread a unique plume fiber through its grain, and hang that tile under a public lantern that stays lit for 28 hours only if the fiber serial is reserved in the ledger. The fee is 13 units, locked until 16 independent peers recompute the fiber hash from the lantern log and the cut timestamp. If two keys share one serial, both fees burn and that lantern is darkened, so a factory of clones pays a rising bill for every extra head instead of reusing a single cheap token.
